correctness.rationale: For a≥1, centers x,y have arm lengths (a,a) and (a,a+1). The graph has n=4a+3 vertices and diameter 2a+2. Starting from uniform colors, the rooted depth-r universal-cover representation (on a tree, the actual truncated rooted tree) shows x and y indistinguishable through depth a and separated at round a+1 by the extra y-arm edge. By that round D_j have unique colors while the three equal-length positions A_i,B_i,C_i remain a triple. At each next round, the split of the predecessor class forces C_{k+1} to separate from A_{k+1},B_{k+1}; a one-step neighborhood argument prevents earlier splits for more distant triples. At round 2a+1 the remaining A_i,B_i pairs are automorphism orbits and all others singletons, hence stable; at 2a last triple intact. Independently coded color refinement for every 1≤a≤40 and checked all 860 asserted middle/subsequent partitions, and all depths. This finite census corroborates the uniform proof, not replaces it.
